title: Act III, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: In the hot afternoon Tybalt seeks Romeo. Romeo, newly married to Tybalt's cousin, refuses to fight. Mercutio fights Tybalt; Romeo steps between them and Tybalt wounds Mercutio under Romeo's arm. Mercutio dies cursing both houses. Romeo kills Tybalt and flees. The Prince banishes Romeo.

contentNotes.teacherNote: Mercutio is fatally wounded and Romeo kills Tybalt on stage. Focus on choices and the honour code, not the swordplay. Alcohol: period drinking appears as social custom (wine at feasts, toasts or 'healths') and as a restorative (aqua vitae, i.e. brandy or spirits). Name it plainly; don't glamorize it. Mercutio mocks a brawler who picks fights 'by the operation of the second cup'.
